transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because… I know this is going to sound strange when I say it out loud, and I’ve been trying to explain it to myself in a way that doesn’t make me sound dramatic, but I’ve been really convinced that two people in my professional circle are sort of… quietly helping direct my career.

One is someone from my MBA program, a classmate, and the other is a startup advisor I know of. It feels like they’re coordinating opportunities for me, but not directly, not like emailing me and saying, “Here, apply to this.” It’s more like certain comments in class, or things that show up in Slack, feel very pointed, like coded signals about where I’m supposed to go next professionally. Like a message will be phrased a certain way, or someone will mention an industry or a company, and it feels too specific to be random.

I know that probably sounds hard to follow. I’m not saying I have, like, a document proving it or anything. But I’ve felt completely convinced that there’s a pattern there, and that they’re communicating indirectly about opportunities I’m meant to notice. It’s been on my mind a lot, and I guess I came in because I’m not sure what to do with that anymore.
Have you had a period where you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah… I think so. It’s less like I’m just “in a good mood” and more like there’s this constant motor running in me. I’ll go from work dashboards to class readings to organizing volleyball stuff, and it feels like stopping would be the weird part. Like I’ll finish one thing and immediately think, okay, what’s the next thing I can knock out?

And sitting still through a normal meeting has been really hard sometimes. Not just boring, but almost physically uncomfortable, like my body is ahead of the room and everyone else is moving too slowly. I find myself wanting to jump in, multitask, check another dashboard, pull up an assignment, text about scheduling—just keep moving. I don’t always think of it as “energized” in a fun way, exactly. It’s more like I can’t find the off switch.
During this time, have you been needing much less sleep than usual and still feeling rested?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that cleanly. I don’t think I’ve been tracking it in a precise way, like writing down hours or anything. There have definitely been nights where I stay up later than I probably should because my mind is still going and I’m trying to finish one more thing, and then one more thing after that.

But whether I’m actually needing “much less” sleep and still feeling rested… I don’t know. Sometimes I wake up and just kind of push straight into the day because there’s stuff to do, not necessarily because I feel rested in a normal, calm way. It’s more like I can keep going. So I guess I’d say I haven’t really noticed it in a clear-cut way, if that makes sense.
Have you heard voices when no one else was there?

Yes… I mean, I think so. That’s one of the things I feel embarrassed saying, because it sounds like a movie version of someone losing touch, and it’s not like that exactly. It’s not a whole conversation or anything.

It happens a few times a week, usually when I’m up late working on school stuff or operations plans, when the apartment is quiet and I’ve been staring at my laptop for too long. I’ll hear my name really clearly, like someone said it right near me, and I’ll look up or check my phone like maybe someone called or texted. Or sometimes it’s just a short phrase, like “go now,” and it feels external enough that I stop what I’m doing and look around the room.

And then there’s nobody there, and nothing on my phone. So I don’t know if that counts as hearing voices, but it’s clear enough in the moment that I react to it like it’s real.
Have you had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

I’m not sure I can say that clearly. I’ve definitely had low days, and stretches where I felt kind of worn down or flat, like I was just getting through what I had to get through. But “most of the day nearly every day for two weeks” feels very specific, and I don’t know that I’ve noticed something that cleanly.

I tend to keep going even when I’m not feeling great, so sometimes it’s hard for me to tell whether I’m actually depressed or just tired or stressed or kind of emotionally drained. I don’t want to say yes if it wasn’t really that consistent. I guess… I haven’t recognized a two-week stretch like that, at least not in a way I could point to confidently.
Have these unusual beliefs or voice-hearing experiences been going on for longer than one month?

Yes… longer than a month. I think it’s been about two months now.

It kind of started around when I began the part-time MBA prerequisite program while still keeping my operations job, and I remember that because my schedule changed so much then. I was trying to juggle work, the classes, the assignments, and just keeping everything organized, so that’s the point in my head where I started noticing these things more.

At first I thought it was just stress or being overtired, so I didn’t really mark it as, like, “this is a thing that’s happening.” But looking back, it hasn’t just been a few days. It’s been going on for roughly two months, give or take.
During this time, have you felt unusually euphoric or on top of the world?

Yes… I think that’s actually a good way to put part of it. Not euphoric like I’m dancing around or happy for no reason exactly, but most days I’ve felt really switched on, like my brain is moving fast and I’m kind of on the edge of something huge. Like there’s this sense that I’m about to pull everything together and it’s all going to lead somewhere important.

It feels optimistic, almost too optimistic compared to how I usually am. I’ll be looking at work stuff or school-related plans and feel like, “Okay, this is it, I can handle all of this, I’m ahead of everyone, I just need to keep going.” And in the moment it doesn’t feel unrealistic, it feels exciting and urgent.

But it’s not all pleasant. I also get irritated really quickly. Like if a teammate is slow to respond, or someone doesn’t understand what I’m asking, I snap more than I normally would. And with my boyfriend, if he delays something small or asks me to slow down, I can get sharp with him, even though later I know it was not worth reacting that strongly. So yes, there’s been this unusually high, “on top of it” feeling, but also this edge to it where little things set me off.
During this period, have you been doing much more goal-directed activity than usual?

Yes, definitely. I mean, that’s one of the things I’ve noticed most, because it’s not just feeling energetic in my head — I’ve actually been starting a lot of things.

At work I’ve been launching extra little projects, like trying to improve processes that honestly weren’t assigned to me. I’ll see something and think, “This needs to be fixed now,” and then I start building a plan or messaging people about it. And for my classes, I’ve been rewriting team processes and trying to turn class assignments into these bigger, more organized systems than they probably need to be.

I’ve also been reaching out to people from networking events much more than I usually would — sending messages, following up, trying to set things up. And then I’ll start organizing everyone’s schedules, like teammates or people around me, because I feel like I can see how everything should fit together.

The problem is, even though it feels productive at the time, I think it’s actually made me drop the ball on some normal follow-through. Like I’ll start three extra things and then miss a basic task I was supposed to finish, or I’ll be so focused on reorganizing the whole system that I don’t complete the actual thing due that day. So yes, I’ve been doing a lot more goal-directed stuff than usual, but it’s not always as useful as it feels in the moment.
Have the voice-hearing experiences happened only during the times when you’ve felt unusually high and driven?

Yes, I think so. I mean… before this whole stretch where I got so energized and driven, I don’t remember anything like that happening.

Before I started the MBA prerequisites and my workload kind of ramped up, I never had this thing where messages felt coded, or like they were meant for me in some hidden way. And I definitely don’t remember hearing my name when nobody was there. That part really seemed to start after my mood shifted and everything got more intense — the classes, work, trying to keep up with all of it, and feeling like I had to keep pushing.

So, as far as I can tell, those experiences have only been happening during this period where I’ve been more “up” and driven. I can’t point to a time before that where it was happening separately.
Has this unusually high or irritable period lasted for at least one week?

Yes, definitely more than a week. It’s been… probably about two months now, honestly. It started around when I began the part-time MBA prerequisite program while still keeping my operations job, and at first I thought it was just me getting into gear or being motivated because I had a lot to manage.

But looking back, it didn’t just last a few days or one stressful week. It’s been this whole stretch since then, where I’ve felt unusually keyed up or driven, and more irritable than I normally am. So yes — at least a week, but really closer to two months.
